questions.question: What does zero-shot cross-lingual transfer mean?
options: Fine-tune a multilingual model on one source language and evaluate on a different language with no target-language labels
Translating without a translation model — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
questions.explanation: Zero-shot transfer: train on the source language, run on the target without target-language supervision.

questions.question: Which model family ships as the standard 100-language cross-lingual baseline?
options: DistilBERT, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
questions.explanation: XLM-R is the canonical 100-language pretrained baseline for cross-lingual classification.

questions.question: Why does English-as-source not always give the best transfer for a non-English target?
options: English has too little data, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence, before defining the measurement, acceptance threshold, or rollback path
Language similarity (typology, script, morphology) predicts transfer quality; a closer high-resource source can outperform English
questions.explanation: Typologically related sources (e.g. Hindi for Indic targets) often outperform English as a fine-tune source.

questions.question: What is the 'fertility tax' for low-resource languages?
options: Low-resource text tokenizes into more subwords per word than English, consuming context window, latency, and capacity
Tokenizers cannot handle Unicode, before defining the measurement, acceptance threshold, or rollback path — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
questions.explanation: Long-tail languages tokenize at much higher fertility, eating context and training efficiency.

questions.question: Why is per-language evaluation required, not aggregated accuracy?
options: Aggregate numbers hide long-tail languages where a multilingual model can be far worse than its mean suggests
Aggregates only work on classification — and applies unchanged even when the lesson's stated preconditions fail
questions.explanation: Aggregate accuracy masks poor performance on low-resource languages; per-language scores expose it.

questions.question: Why is fine-tuning learning rate critical when adapting a multilingual model with few-shot data?
options: It changes the vocabulary, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence
High LR can collapse the multilingual alignment and effectively reduce the model to English-only
questions.explanation: Excessive LR drifts the shared representation; conservative LR (~2e-5) preserves cross-lingual structure.
